title: Replace the screen on a front-entry phone
tools: Heat pad, or heat gun on its lowest setting
Tray or mat to keep screws in order
parts: Replacement screen made for your exact phone model
New screen adhesive made for your phone

diyCheck.summary: This is a sample guide for learning the general method on a front-entry phone. Your phone's layout may differ, so also check a guide written for your exact model.
goToShopIf: The battery is swollen or the screen is being pushed up from inside
The phone has been in water or has burn marks
The phone holds data you cannot back up
You do not have a replacement screen made for your exact model
The phone has an in-screen fingerprint reader and you cannot confirm it will work with the new screen

steps.title: Prepare the phone and your workspace
steps.body: Back up your data if the phone still lets you. Let the battery run down to below 25% if you can. Power the phone off fully, unplug it and remove the SIM tray. Clear a table of anything that can burn.
warnings: Do not start this repair on a bed, sofa or carpet.
checklist: Data is backed up, or you accept it may be lost
Phone is powered off and unplugged
SIM tray is removed
Safety glasses are on

steps.title: Tape over cracked glass
steps.body: If the glass is cracked, cover the whole screen with overlapping strips of clear packing tape. The tape holds loose pieces together and helps the suction cup grip.
warnings: Wear gloves and eye protection whenever you handle broken glass.
checklist: Cracked areas are fully covered with tape

steps.title: Remove the bottom screws
steps.body: Many front-entry phones have two small screws on the bottom edge. Remove them and keep them in order on your tray. If you see no screws, check a guide for your exact model before going further.
checklist: Screws are laid out in order

steps.title: Warm the screen edges
steps.body: Warm the bottom edge in short passes, keeping the heat moving. Stop when the glass feels too hot to keep your finger on it, and let it cool a little before heating again.
warnings: Too much heat can permanently damage the screen and the battery behind it. Keep heat on the edges.
The glass can burn your skin. Handle it with care.
checklist: Heat stayed on the edges
Glue feels softer at the edge

diyGate.question: This step uses heat on a phone with a lithium battery directly behind the screen. Check the phone first.
stopIf: The screen is bulging or being pushed up from inside
The phone feels hot while switched off
You can smell a sweet or chemical odor from the phone

steps.title: Lift the screen
steps.body: Press the suction cup near the bottom edge and pull up gently to open a small gap. Slide a plastic pick in at a shallow angle, then work it slowly along the sides, adding picks to hold the seam open. Open the screen only a little, because its cables are short.
warnings: Insert the pick only a few millimeters. Deeper can tear the display cables.
Never use a metal tool here.
checklist: Adhesive is released all the way around
Screen was not pulled against its cables

diyGate.question: Once you lift the screen, the phone's waterproofing is gone and the display cables are exposed.
stopIf: The glass is breaking apart instead of lifting in one piece
You cannot tell where the display cables are

steps.title: Disconnect the battery
steps.body: Open the screen just enough to reach inside, and support it so it does not hang by its cables. Remove the small bracket over the connectors and keep its screws in order. Lift the battery connector straight up with a plastic spudger, and do this before touching any other connector.
warnings: Use plastic only. A metal tool can short the connector and cause sparks.
checklist: Battery connector is unplugged
Connector cannot spring back onto the socket

steps.title: Remove the old screen
steps.body: Lift each display connector straight up with the spudger. Set the old screen aside with its glass side down, on a surface where nobody will lean on it.
warnings: Lift connectors from their edges. Prying from one corner can bend the socket pins.
checklist: All display connectors are unplugged
Old screen is set aside safely

steps.title: Clean the frame and move small parts
steps.body: Remove old adhesive from the frame with a plastic tool and a little isopropyl alcohol, then let it dry completely. If the new screen did not come with an earpiece mesh or sensor bracket, carefully move them from the old screen.
warnings: Isopropyl alcohol is flammable. Keep it away from heat tools.
checklist: Frame is clean and dry
Small parts are moved to the new screen

steps.title: Test the new screen before sealing
steps.body: Connect the new screen's cables first, then connect the battery. Do not press the screen down yet. Power on and check the picture, the brightness and touch across the whole screen. Power off and disconnect the battery again when you finish.
warnings: Always unplug the battery before plugging or unplugging display cables.
checklist: Picture has no lines or dark patches
Touch works in every area
Battery is disconnected again

steps.title: Seal the phone
steps.body: Apply the new adhesive to the frame. Reconnect the battery, refit the bracket and its screws, then lower the screen and press it evenly into place. Refit the bottom screws and the SIM tray. Hold the screen with light, even pressure while the adhesive sets.
warnings: After opening, the phone may no longer be water resistant.
checklist: Screen sits flat all the way around
All screws are back in place
Phone powers on

steps.title: Dispose of the old screen safely
steps.body: Wrap the old screen in tape or thick paper so nobody gets cut, then take it to an e-waste collection point. Many repair shops accept old parts.
checklist: Old screen is wrapped
Table is clear of glass pieces
